    Vennerian Channel Wardens¶

    [!INFO] The Toll Wardens — Every Hull Pays Between Xeti Sea and Beast's Bay they built a gate in the water — and then became the gate.

    History¶

    The military-maritime order of the Vennerian Trade Republic — the sea-trade superpower of South Erisdar whose constructed Vennerian Channel linking the Xeti Sea to Beast's Bay is the busiest chokepoint on Ge'or. The Wardens are the force that makes "Venner controls passage — every ship pays" a true sentence rather than a boast.

    Formally chartered after the channel's cut (the labor that dammed and dredged between Xeti and Marti is its own dark chapter — Venner chronicles call it engineering), the Wardens garrison the channel gates, the twin forts at its mouths, and the Vennerian colonies that secure its approaches: Mia Checkpoint on Mia island, Goishi on Lumina, New Venner and Johannstadt (ex-Taberis, taken 524 AGD) in Dissenbarg, Love of the Sea in Kutten, and the Vennerian Channel (Marti) and Vennerian Aelefer Channel sister cuts.

    In 544 AGD the Wardens provided the marines for the invasion of Minir island — taking Neopao and Koln and reducing Dukedam to puppet — a reminder that toll-collectors can become conquerors when the toll is empire.

    Patron¶

    The Vennerian Trade Republic Senate of Sea-Lords — plutocrats who own the toll. Wardens swear to the Channel itself as legal person: their oath is witnessed by a pour of seawater taken from the Channel's midpoint, kept in a stoppered vial until discharge. Ship chaplains of any faith may ride, but the Wardens' own ritual is accounting: the toll-book is read aloud each change of watch, and a warden who cannot balance it is relieved before he is rebuked.

    Venner is slowly integrating the Corinite League and turning Dissenbarg cities into tributaries; where negotiations stall, the Wardens are the patient hint: the Channel can also close.

    Sigil¶

    A white ship's prow over black channel gates on a sea-blue field, the gates rendered as a Vennerian Ducat on its edge — prow obverse, gates reverse. Command pennants add a Silver Bride-silver thread at the hoist, because Venner claims the ring itself pays toll at night (a joke told only offshore).

    Role¶

    Maritime chokepoint control, toll enforcement, and naval infantry. The Wardens field gate artillery, chain crews, boarding pikes, and the finest light marines on Ge'or for the specific business of taking a ship intact enough to tax it again. They do not seek open sea battle against the Anos Plutocracy's second-rate-but-still-dangerous fleet unless forced — they seek position: control of Mia means control of Lumina resupply, control of Goishi means sight over Beast's Bay, control of the gates means control of price.

    Inland Venner factors quote prices in Erilia and convert to Ducats at predatory spreads; the Wardens ensure no captain evades the spread by running the channel under cover.

    Relation to Currencies & Regions¶

    The Wardens are the living backing of the Vennerian Ducat — pale sea-gold dusted with Romanium, not valuable because it is scarce but because every hull between Erisdar and Dissenbarg must buy it to pass. The coin is Ducat-or-nothing at the gates; no Anosi Mark plate, no Meblean Pearl hoop, no Silver Talon will open them.

    Consequently the busiest honest market on Ge'or is the exchange outside the gates where Anosi factors grudgingly buy Ducats from Vennerian money changers who will, hours later, grudgingly accept Anosi plates for Beast's Bay provisions — the whole Anos-Venner trade race rendered as queue. The Wardens also control Demon's Horn traders' access westward and take their Ducat there too.
